question:
The following pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in manufacturing a certain product. Study the pie chart and answer the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/906e77e813976886aa67d24f903e81dedfd7187975fbcecf1f7820ecbbd6e2e1.png] 

If 500 products are manufactured and the direct labour cost on them amounts to Rs. 62,500, then what should be the selling price of the product so that manufacturer can earn a profit of 50%?
solution:
**Given:**

 
• Number of products = 500
 
• Direct labor cost= Rs.62500
 
• Profit percentage =50%

**Formula used:**

 
• Profit\: percentage ={Profitover Cost\: price}×100
 
• Profit= selling price- cost price

**Calculation:**

Let x be the total cost price of 500 products.

We know that,

Direct labour cost is 30% of the total cost price of 500 products,

30\%× x = 62500\ {30over100}× x=62500\ x={62500× 100over 30}\ x=208333.33

The cost price of one product is,

= (x)/(500)

= (208333.33)/(500)

= 416.67

Now,

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + Profit%)/100

Selling price = 416.67 × (100 + 50)/100 = 625

Selling price = Rs. 625

Therefore, **the correct answer is option 3.**
